finalText:
It's a small five-file Node server with no outside dependencies. Here's how a request flows through it:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
    A -->|passes request| C[routes.js]
    C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
    C -->|writes| E[store.js]
    D -->|misses go to| E
```

- **`server.js`** opens the HTTP port and checks every request for a valid token before anything else runs.
- **`auth.js`** makes those tokens. Each one is a user ID plus a signed stamp, checked with a timing-safe compare so no one can guess a valid one bit by bit.
- **`routes.js`** is the small table of what each URL does. Reads (`GET /users`, `GET /orders`) go through the cache. The write (`POST /orders`) skips it and goes straight to the store.
- **`cache.js`** is a 256-slot memory cache that keeps recent reads around so the store isn't hit every time.
- **`store.js`** holds the actual data in memory. Nothing sticks around forever — each record quietly expires 15 minutes after it was last written.

One thing worth knowing early on: this store is in-memory only, so a restart wipes everything. It reads like a stand-in for a real database that hasn't been built yet.
